decisions.text: type pie: fractions of the total are the message: a pie, which shows ½, ⅓ and ¼ at a glance and announces the whole (G1.36)
slices in their order, clockwise from 12 o'clock: Very high risk, High risk, Moderate risk, Low risk, Very low risk
the parts are ordered: steps of one hue, darker for each part from the last to the first, the first at 12 o'clock (G4.7; each slice still its own colour, G7.25)
each slice its own colour, in steps of one hue in their order: Very high risk seq-9, High risk seq-8, Moderate risk seq-6, Low risk seq-5, Very low risk seq-3
each slice named outside it, its value under the name, formatted as one set (G7.27, D-51 (ii)): 23%, 21%, 38%, 16%, 2%
leaders to Low risk, Very low risk (a zero, a slice under 8°, or a label moved from its place; G7.29, D-34)
no outlines: true gaps 1.0 pt wide between the slices (G7.26s: 0.7 % of the diameter)

source.notes: 00-01 F3; 13-15 F10 (the aggressive portfolio's data, s. 0020, 0368); 07 R7-35
source.shows: ours, from the book's data, which it draws as 100 % stacks: one total of ordered parts as a pie, the risk levels in their own order from 12 o'clock rather than largest first (R7-35, G7.28), in steps of one hue, the first the darkest, rather than a hue each (G4.7, R3-8), as the book's good stacks (P3-34); Very low risk, under 8°, pointed to by a leader (G7.29)
